While they are wrapped in double quotes, an attacker who controls the search query can inject quote characters into self.tokens.field[0] or self.tokens.fieldname to break out of the quotes and inject arbitrary SQL. The to_sql() method builds SQL by concatenating these values directly: e.g., line 144 uses f'%({p})s=ANY("{self.tokens.field[0]}")' where self.tokens.field[0] comes from the parsed query without validation.
findings.suggested_fix: Parameterize column identifiers using PostgreSQL's identifier parameter mechanism or implement a strict allowlist of permitted field names that gets validated against before use in SQL generation. Alternatively, use an ORM layer that handles identifier escaping properly, or use identifier quoting with proper escaping of double quotes in field names (e.g., replacing '"' with '""' in PostgreSQL).

Release 9 only supports Python 3.9 or higher.

- Postgres version 13 or better
- MongoDB version 6.0 or better

Installation
------------

To install MongoDB on Debian/Ubuntu run:

    $ sudo apt-get install -y mongodb-org
    $ mongod

To install MongoDB on CentOS/RHEL run:

    $ sudo yum install -y mongodb
    $ mongod

    $ alertad run

    $ tar zxvf alerta-webui.tar.gz
    $ cd dist
    $ python3 -m http.server 8000

### Docker

-------------

To configure the ``alertad`` server override the default settings in ``/etc/alertad.conf``
or using ``ALERTA_SVR_CONF_FILE`` environment variable::

    $ ALERTA_SVR_CONF_FILE=~/.alertad.conf
